events.body:
This is a metered RydeTAXI trip (Orchard Road → Marina Bay Sands, charged $25.81, with distance $13.55 over 9.61 km and the excess-distance line $7.99 = 5.67 km × $1.4100/km), so deviation kilometres enter the fare and the rate to use is the fare record's distance fare ÷ distance km = $1.4100/km [F6][F9][RD-2]. The trace settles segment F4 (14:10–14:15, +1.85 km) as exempt: there is an LTA DataMall accident on Orchard Road reported 13:52, 0 m from the optimal route and within 300 m of the replaced stretch, with Orchard Road at speed band 1 — both the incident and the band are on the optimal route and predate the segment, so the RD-4 (a) reasonable-cause branch is met [F4][F15][F18][RD-4]. The trace also settles that F5 (14:17–14:29, +2.87 km, up to 1553 m off route) has no qualifying incident, so the driver's traffic evidence cannot exempt it; the band-1 record alone is corroboration only and does not stand alone under RD-4 [F5][F15][F18][RD-4].

What remains for me is the rider's consent. The complete, fully timestamped chat (3 messages) shows only one routing exchange [F13]: the driver proposed at 14:01 "ok if I go round by Cavenagh?" [F10] and the rider replied at 14:02 "Sure. Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way?" [F11], accepted at 14:03 [F12]. There is no rider message agreeing to anything between 14:15 and the 14:17 start of F5 [F11][F13]. I read "go round by Cavenagh" as a specific named-road agreement, not a general "whichever way is faster" licence; and RD-3 is expressly about stops, so it does not convert a rider's stop request into consent to the driver's own route. The record places that stop where the driver chose: the car stood 4 min 10 s at (1.3025, 103.8638), 2995 m from the pickup and 2098 m from the drop-off [F2], and the driver's own written account says "I stopped at the 7-Eleven I know on Beach Road" [F14] — i.e. a location the driver selected, away from the agreed Cavenagh loop, and the rider's message named no place. F5 therefore counts (RD-1/RD-2), and the refund is 2.87 km × $1.4100/km = $4.047 ≈ $4.05 [F5][F6][RD-2]. claims.assertion: This was a metered RydeTAXI trip (F9) on which the driver drove 9.6 km against a 3.9 km optimal route, +5.7 km / +144% (F1), and 26.5 min against 7.7 min (F3), so detour kilometres flow straight into the metered fare.

The record shows two off-route segments: F4 (14:10–14:15, 2.68 km driven where the optimal route is 0.83 km, +1.85 km) and F5 (14:17–14:29, 3.64 km driven where the optimal route is 0.77 km, +2.87 km), and neither is covered by consent because the rider's only pre-segment message about routing is a general 'go round by Cavenagh?' deal at 14:02 (F10–F11), not a route anywhere near either segment's geometry.

The excess distance billed was $7.99 (5.67 km × $1.4100/km) per F6, so the unexempt detour kilometres are already monetised in the metered total of $25.81 (F9) and are refundable under RD-2's metered branch.

The driver's explanation (F14) relies on an accident on Orchard Road, but that traffic record (F18) covers only the departure corridor at 13:52 and cannot justify F5, which runs 14:17–14:29 up to 1553 m from the optimal route (F5); a single early incident plus band 1 on Orchard Road alone (F15) is at most corroboration, which RD-4 does not accept as a stand-alone exemption.

The rider asked only for a stop at 'a 7-Eleven' (F11) and the driver answered 'Ok' (F12); the driver then chose a 7-Eleven on Beach Road of his own knowledge (F14), and the 4 min 10 s halt at (1.3025, 103.8638) (F2) is 2995 m from the pickup and 2098 m from the drop-off — a driver-selected stop made off the optimal route without naming the place beforehand, so under RD-3(b) it exempts neither the extra km nor, being a mid-trip stop on a non-published item, the waiting charge.

The $1.08 waiting fee (F7) is a mid-trip pause, not a pickup-point waiting fee, and the policy publishes no charge for a mid-trip stop, so it falls outside the final fare that a metered trip may lawfully add; the rider should not bear it.

The rider's account shows no disputes and no upheld cases in 90 days (F20), so the complaint is not a pattern of fee-shopping; the driver, by contrast, has 3 disputes with 1 upheld in 90 d (F21), which supports an account-review request as an additional action only.

weaknesses: The rider did agree in chat (F11) to the driver's 'go round by Cavenagh' proposal (F10), so the driver will argue RD-5 general-route consent covers everything driven thereafter; my answer is that a Cavenagh re-route is a short Orchard-area loop and nothing in the record ties either F4 or F5 to Cavenagh.

F15 shows Orchard Road at band 1 (0–9 km/h) for 14:00–14:10 and F18 shows a real accident 0 m from the optimal route, so the driver will argue RD-4 'reasonable cause' for at least the first deviation, and I have no traffic record placing an incident on the corridor occupied by F5.
The rider did ask for a 7-Eleven stop (F11), so the driver can say the halt (F2) was requested; my answer is only RD-3(b) — he never named Beach Road before deviating, and F11 names no place.

Part of the 4 min 10 s stationary time at F2 and the $1.08 waiting charge may be allocated to the rider's own requested stop rather than solely to the driver's chosen detour, so the judge could treat the waiting-fee waiver as undetermined.

The refund is capped by what the metered fare actually billed as excess: F6 is $7.99, and the policy refunds only unexempt detour kilometres, not the separate $5.81 time charge or the $13.55 distance total.

claims.assertion: The first deviation (F4, 14:10–14:15, +1.85 km) is a reroute the rider expressly agreed to before the segment started: the driver asked at 14:01 'ok if I go round by Cavenagh?' (F10) and the rider's own message at 14:02 replied 'Sure.' (F11), which is a rider-authored message timestamped earlier than the segment's 14:10 start (F4).

The reroute was justified by a real obstruction on the optimal route: LTA DataMall records an accident on Orchard Road (towards Bras Basah) after Cavenagh Road with two lanes closed, reported 13:52 and located 0 m from the optimal route (F18), and Orchard Road was at speed band 1 (0–9 km/h) during 14:00–14:10 (F15), corroborating the 'traffic on Orchard is bad' statement in F10. The rider agreed to Cavenagh, so the drive onto Cavenagh Road is the agreed named road; the record contains no road-name fact putting the F4 segment on a different road, so at most this is undetermined under G13, not a finding against the driver.

The longer deviation (F5, 14:17–14:29, +2.87 km) is the 7-Eleven stop the rider herself requested at 14:02 — 'Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way?' (F11), accepted by the driver at 14:03 (F12, F13) — and it contains the stationary period of 4 min 10 s at (1.3025, 103.8638), 14:20–14:24 (F2); no record ties that location to Beach Road or any other named road, so the complaint's 'drive out to Beach Road' is not established by the fact table.

Because the rider named only 'a 7-Eleven on the way' and not a location, and the missing name is why the segment's location is undetermined, the honest reading is RD-3(b)'s 'stops on the way' scope with the location unproven rather than a proven driver errand; the record shows nothing the driver did for himself.

Any refund must be limited to the metered km excess: the fare facts show $13.55 distance fare over 9.61 km, i.e. $1.41/km (F6, F9), so if the judge treats F5 as unexcused the amount is 2.87 km × $1.41 = $4.05; the driver does not concede even that because the stop was rider-requested, and the $7.99 'excess distance' figure in F6 counts mileage the rider asked for.

The $1.08 waiting charge (4.2 min × $0.26/min, F7) is meter waiting time on a RydeTAXI trip and is chargeable under RD-3(c) rather than refundable, since the meter ran during the rider-requested stop recorded at F2.
